thread:
maria: Heads up — after last night's runtime rollout (kernel heuristics + quant-profile v2) we've seen prefix cache hit-rate drop on a subset of customer traffic. quick summary: 18% -> 6% early-prefix hits for short priming prompts (<=64 tokens).

alex: ugh. any obvious log lines? which kernel flag rolled?

maria: flag is `kernel.variant=hybrid-attn-v3` + quant profile `qv2` enabled on the canary pool. attaching a minimal repro in logs:
```
-- request id: req-3b9a
-- model: opt-13b-qv2
-- prefix_key: ctx_v1:0x4f2a1b:len24
-- runtime kernel: hybrid-attn-v3 build=2024-11-09
-- cache lookup: false
-- expected key (old): ctx_v1:0x4f2a1b:len24
-- observed key (new): ctx_v1:0x4f2a1b\u0000:len24
```

sam: wait, there's a null char in the observed key? that smells like a padding/serialization change in the new kernel.

lena: exact symptom we saw during the attn-tiling experiment last quarter. kernel changed how it serializes token offsets when fused-attn enabled. keys no longer canonical across variants.

perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate drop 18.2% -> 5.9% (p95 latency delta +6ms on priming flows). impacted pool: canary-gpu-pool-3.

alex: do we have any sha/build mismatch evidence? Could be a mismatch between compile flags that change padding of kv blobs.

maria: yes — heap of small diffs in profiler: `kv_serialize()` now appends a 0x00 separator for tiled-attn. Old path didn't. That changes the string fingerprint used for prefix lookup.

sam: quick mitigation: normalize keys during lookup by stripping trailing \u0000 and whitespace. but that is a bandaid — would be safer to keep serialization stable across kernels.

lena: agreed. short-term mitigation: runtime config `prefix_key_normalize=true` to strip NUL and trailing padding on lookup only. Long-term: unify `kv_serialize()` across kernels or add a canonicalization layer before cache insert.

maria: collected 1200 trace examples where the same user prompt generated two different keys pre/post roll. I'll upload to /tmp/prefix-repro-3729.tar.gz. repro script: `scripts/repro_prefix_mismatch.sh --pool canary-gpu-pool-3 --sample 100`

alex: can we safely flip `prefix_key_normalize` in prod? what's the perf cost?

perf-bot: cost-estimate: normalization adds ~0.8us per lookup (string trim) — measured on canary: negligible overall but helps hit-rate.

sam: also saw that batching heuristics changed — continuous-batching now groups by `kernel.variant` first which separated previously coalesced requests. that reduced prefix reuse in the batch window. two separate problems stacked.

maria: exact. observed batching window (20ms) previously coalesced mixed kernel-variant requests; new scheduler prefers kernel-affinity causing many small batches and fewer shared caches per batch.

lena: proposed action items:
- revert kernel.variant change on canary pool (rollback) — immediate rollback if customer-facing regression persists.
- enable `prefix_key_normalize=true` across canary and staging ASAP.
- run targeted end-to-end A/B with identical traffic and compare hit maps.
- add unit tests for `kv_serialize()` cross-kernel parity.

alex: I'll open a rollback PR for the canary pool and pin quant profile to qv1 while we triage. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/rollbacks/3729

maria: +1. also need a small patch to the prefix cache lookup to do a tolerant compare: first exact, then normalized lookup before miss path. I can draft.

sam: for root cause we should capture:
- diff of `kv_serialize()` between builds (git/objdump)
- example keys before/after for 1000 samples
- batching assignment logs for the same request id shards
- perf counters for cache lookup time pre/post

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback-canary-3729 by alex. ETA 7m.

lena: timeline: if rollback completes and hit-rate recovers -> we know kernel serialization change is primary. if rollback doesn't recover fully -> batching heuristics change is likely contributing heavily.

maria: collecting additional artifacts now and will link a small corpus under the bug ticket. also adding a short-run smoke job to validate normalization patch doesn't introduce false positives (two different contexts becoming conflated).

alex: FYI ops, can you pin affected customers to dedicated capacity if they call in? avoids noisy canary traffic mixing.

sam: I'll start writing unit tests for cross-kernel canonicalization and a lightweight fuzz harness to ensure no collisions when we strip padding.

maria: thanks team. next updates in this thread. I'll post the repro link after upload. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: customers with heavy priming flows may see token-cost increase if warmup hit-rate stays low — consider outreach to top 5 impacted accounts.

lena: added owner label: eng-runtime/prefix-cache-bakeoff. ticket: RED-7821.

maria: upload done: /artifacts/RED-7821/prefix-repro-3729.tar.gz (contains repro script + 1200 trace pairs + simple validator).

alex: rollback finished, canary pool back to `hybrid-attn-v2` + `qv1`. monitoring…

perf-bot: post-rollback metric: prefix_hit_rate back to 17.6% (baseline 18.2%). p95 latency back within 1ms of baseline.

maria: great. keeping normalization patch in PR for the extra safety net. will follow up with a postmortem once we verify fixes and add tests.

sam: note for postmortem: call out two failure modes stacking (serialization change + kernel-affinity batching) so we add both checks to rollout playbook.

lena: thanks all. closing loop once postmortem is up.
